key: Two shopkeepers on the same street in Chennai
name: ch05_two_saree_shops
alt: Two saree shops side by side on one street: a bored owner in a shiny empty showroom on the left, a smiling owner offering coffee to a family in a cramped busy shop on the right.
scene: A street-level split view of two saree shops next to each other on a busy Chennai street, divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT half: a gleaming showroom with a glass front, polished marble floor, a small wall air-conditioner and neat glass shelves of folded silk sarees in bright colours. The owner (about 45, crisp white shirt, gold watch) sits behind a long glass counter, slumped, eyes on his phone, mouth in a bored flat frown. The showroom is empty; a family at the doorway is already turning away, a small dashed arrow pointing them out and towards the right half. RIGHT half: a narrow cramped shop with wooden shelves stacked to the ceiling with silk sarees in teal, maroon and gold. The owner (about 55, white veshti and half-sleeve shirt, sandalwood mark on forehead) has stood up from his stool, smiling widely, one hand waving the family in and the other holding out a small steel tumbler of filter coffee with a curl of steam. A family (mother in a green saree, father, teenage daughter) sit on a low bench, the mother holding up a saree to the light and smiling. Warm afternoon light; the left side cool and still, the right side warm and lively. Labels: "BORED" above the left shop, "WELCOME" above the right shop.

name: ch05_train_toddler_biscuit
alt: Inside a crowded night-train bay, a toddler on her mother's lap offers a biscuit to a grumpy uncle opposite, who laughs and takes it while the others start sharing oranges.
scene: An inside view of one bay of a crowded Indian second-class sleeper compartment at night, seen from the corridor. Two facing lower berths with blue rexine seats, an upper berth with a folded blanket, a barred window showing a dark sky and a few passing lights, a small yellow ceiling lamp. LEFT berth: a young mother (late 20s, printed cotton salwar, dupatta over her shoulder) holds a toddler girl (about 2, pigtails, pink frock) on her lap. The toddler leans forward, beaming, holding out a half-eaten soggy biscuit with a little crumb trail. RIGHT berth: a heavy-set uncle (about 60, grey moustache, half-sleeve checked shirt, dhoti) who had been frowning with arms crossed now leans in laughing, one hand reaching for the biscuit. A small grumpy-face inset bubble behind him shows how he looked a minute ago, with an arrow to his laughing face now. Beside them a college boy lowers his phone and grins, and an older woman by the window is peeling an orange, handing segments across; a few orange peels on the small fold-out table. A dashed curve of hearts and orange segments links the people in the bay. Warm lamp light against the blue night outside, tired but cosy mood. Label: "ONE SMILE" in the upper left corner above the toddler.

key: a distant uncle you have met twice greets you
name: ch05_wedding_two_smiles
alt: At a wedding, a warm uncle holds a young man's hands and asks about his mother, while an insurance agent with an identical grin slips him a business card.
scene: A split illustration set in a colourful Indian wedding hall with marigold garlands, a decorated stage and plastic chairs in the background, divided by a thin vertical line, the same young man (late 20s, cream kurta) appearing in both halves. LEFT half: a distant uncle (about 65, white kurta, Nehru jacket, thick spectacles, grey hair) holds the young man's hand in both of his, head tilted, eyes crinkled in a real smile; a small speech bubble above shows a tiny knee with a bandage and a question mark, standing for the question about the mother's knee. A small heart floats between them. RIGHT half: an insurance agent (about 40, shiny shirt, slicked hair, lanyard) smiles equally wide, showing all his teeth, but his eyes look at the young man's pocket while one hand slides a white business card into it; a small rupee symbol floats above the card. The young man leans back slightly with a polite fixed smile. Both smiles are drawn with exactly the same mouth curve to show same muscles, different message. Festive warm light, marigold orange and gold everywhere. Labels: "MEANS IT" above the left half, "SELLING" above the right half.

key: You call two Bengaluru restaurants to book a table
name: ch05_phone_booking_voices
alt: A young woman on her phone hears two restaurant staff: a sighing, flat voice from one and a bright, warm voice from a smiling receptionist at the other.
scene: A three-part composition. In the CENTRE foreground a young woman (about 28, kurti and jeans) sits on a sofa at home with her phone to her ear, a small calendar on the side table with a heart drawn around a date for her parents' anniversary. Two curved dashed lines run from her phone to two small scenes above her. UPPER LEFT: a dim restaurant back counter where a staff member (about 30, black T-shirt, headset) slouches with his chin on his hand, eyes rolled up, flipping a booking register with a bored sigh shown as a little grey puff; the sound line from him to the woman is a flat, straight grey zigzag. UPPER RIGHT: a bright reception desk with a small plant and fairy lights where a receptionist (about 25, neat uniform shirt, hair tied back) smiles warmly into a desk phone, pointing to a corner table on a seating chart with a small star; the sound line from her to the woman is a smooth warm curved wave with tiny notes on it. The woman's face is turned slightly towards the warm side, smiling. Neither restaurant face is visible to her, shown by the dashed lines passing through a small phone icon. Evening indoor light. Labels: "FLAT" next to the left sound line, "WARM" next to the right sound line.

key: A young chef opens a small biryani place in Hyderabad
name: ch05_biryani_chef_then_now
alt: The same chef in two moments: early on, smiling and serving biryani to regulars in a busy small eatery; years later, alone in an office buried in invoices, frowning.
scene: A split before-and-after illustration divided by a thin vertical line, the same woman chef in both halves. LEFT half: a small cheerful biryani eatery with four tables, a big copper handi on the counter with steam rising. The chef (about 28, white chef coat, hair in a bun, bright smile) stands by a table ladling biryani onto a plate for a pair of regulars, an older man and a college girl, who laugh and give a thumbs-up; a short queue is visible at the doorway spilling onto the street. A small heart floats over the handi. RIGHT half: a cramped back office with a desk piled with papers, a laptop showing a roster grid, a calculator and a wall chart of three branch pins. The same chef, five years older (tired eyes, coat swapped for a plain office shirt), sits hunched with a hand on her forehead, frowning, a phone pressed to her ear. A tiny window in the office wall shows the dining room with empty chairs and one regular looking at his plate, a small question mark above his head. The light on the left is warm and golden, on the right cool and grey. Labels: "THEN" above the left half, "NOW" above the right half.

key: An engineer in a Pune housing society has
name: ch05_society_good_morning
alt: A software engineer walks past a society guard with eyes on his phone on Monday; by Friday he greets everyone and the guard opens the gate for him while a neighbour waves.
scene: A split before-and-after illustration of the entrance of a Pune housing society: a sliding iron gate, a small security cabin, a row of parked cars and a lift lobby behind, divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT half: the engineer (about 32, office shirt, laptop backpack, earphones) walks past head down, eyes glued to his phone, mouth flat. The security guard (about 50, khaki uniform, cap) sits in the cabin looking away, the car-wash boy (about 17, shorts, bucket and cloth) wipes a car without looking up, and the gate stays shut. RIGHT half: the same engineer, phone in his pocket, walks upright smiling and waving, a small speech bubble with a waving hand and a sun icon for his greeting. The guard is already standing, smiling, pulling the gate open for him with a small arrow showing it sliding. The car-wash boy grins and points at the engineer's freshly washed car first in the row, with a little sparkle. On the balcony above, a neighbour (about 45, kurta) leans over the railing waving and holding a small paper flyer with a diya on it, the Diwali committee invite. Morning sunlight. Labels: "MONDAY" above the left half, "FRIDAY" above the right half.

key: A kirana shop owner wakes up on a festival morning
name: ch05_kirana_festival_morning
alt: A kirana shop owner with a grey storm cloud over his head pulls up the shutter on Diwali morning; by the fifth customer his forced smile has become a real one and the cloud is gone.
scene: A wide view of a small Indian kirana shop front on Diwali morning, shown as a sequence from left to right. Strings of marigolds and a small row of diyas line the shop step; shelves behind hold rice sacks, biscuit packets and jars. FAR LEFT: the shopkeeper (about 50, half-sleeve shirt, lungi, spectacles pushed up) is pulling up the rolling steel shutter with one hand while rubbing his temple with the other, eyes tired; a small grey rain cloud with a jagged line hovers over his head. CENTRE: behind the counter he lights an agarbatti, a curl of smoke rising, and a small radio beside him shows musical notes; he greets the first customer, an aunty in a bright saree with a shopping bag, with a wide but stiff smile, the grey cloud above him now half the size. RIGHT: a little later, he laughs while handing a packet of sweets to a fifth customer, a young father with a child holding a sparkler; the cloud has turned into a small sun. A row of five small numbered customer dots along the bottom edge with an arrow running from 1 to 5 shows time passing. Bright festive morning light. Labels: "ACTING" above the centre greeting, "REAL" above the right-hand scene.

key: Two auto-rickshaw drivers wait in the same queue
name: ch05_two_auto_drivers
alt: Two auto-rickshaw drivers in the same heat outside a railway station: one scowling and cursing in his seat, the other humming with a chai and joking with a passenger.
scene: A street-level split view of an auto-rickshaw queue outside a big Mumbai railway station on a hot June afternoon, the station's arched facade faint in the background, a blazing sun at the top centre shining on both halves equally, divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT half: a yellow-and-black auto-rickshaw, its driver (about 45, khaki uniform shirt, towel round his neck) slumped in the seat, brow knotted, fist raised, a small speech bubble with angry scribble symbols aimed at a traffic signal and a phone showing an app screen with a red cross. Sweat drops fly from his face. RIGHT half: an identical auto-rickshaw, its driver (about 50, same khaki uniform, small cap) leans back relaxed holding a small glass of chai, musical notes rising from a little radio on the dashboard; a chaiwala with a kettle stands beside him laughing at a joke, and a passenger (young woman with a suitcase) is climbing in, smiling. Same heat lines rise from the road in both halves, and the same meter on both autos shows the same fare. Labels: "GRUMBLES" above the left half, "HUMS" above the right half.

key: A new student joins a hostel in Delhi
name: ch05_hostel_filter_coffee
alt: A shy new student steps into a lively hostel common room holding a big flask of filter coffee and steel cups, smiling and introducing herself, and the others turn towards her.
scene: A wide view of a girls' hostel common room in Delhi in the evening: a carrom board on a low table, a sagging sofa, a television on a wall shelf, a notice board with pinned flyers, warm tube light. On the LEFT, in the doorway, a new student (about 19, simple kurta, hair in a long plait, a small flower clip) steps in holding a large steel flask of filter coffee in one hand and a stack of small steel tumblers in the other, smiling shyly but bravely; a small speech bubble beside her shows a coffee cup and the number "14". Behind her, a dim corridor with her room door marked "14" is shown in cool blue, the empty side she is leaving. On the RIGHT, three students around the carrom board (one in a hoodie, one in a T-shirt and track pants, one with spectacles) have looked up from their game and are turning towards her with surprised, welcoming smiles, one already holding out a hand for a cup. A dashed arrow runs from the doorway into the warm, lit circle around the carrom board. In the top corner a small inset shows the same girl later, laughing, holding a clipboard in front of a rangoli and a banana-leaf lunch for the Onam night. Label: "GOES FIRST" at the top centre above the doorway.

key: two medical shops side by side
name: ch05_two_chemists
alt: Two chemist shops side by side selling the same tablet at the same price: one owner slaps the strip down without looking up, the other kindly explains the dose, and a queue forms at his counter.
scene: A street-level view of two small neighbourhood medical shops side by side under one long awning, each with a green cross sign without any words, a glass counter and shelves of medicine boxes behind. LEFT shop: the chemist (about 40, grey shirt, reading glasses low on his nose) looks down at his phone, one hand slapping a strip of tablets onto the counter, the other pointing at a price tag; a young man customer stands stiffly, wallet out, unsmiling. Nobody else waits there. RIGHT shop: the chemist (about 55, white shirt, kind face, spectacles) leans across the counter, smiling, holding up the same strip of tablets and pointing at a small drawing of a plate and a glass of water to show take after food and drink water; the customer, a worried mother holding a child's hand, nods with relief. Behind her stands a short queue of three people (an elderly man with a cloth bag, a college girl, a man in a helmet). Both strips are identical white-and-blue tablets and both have the same small price tag reading "30" to show the price is the same. Afternoon light. Labels: "SAME PRICE" centred at the top between the two shops, "QUEUE" above the line at the right shop.

key: It is 11 p.m. at a Swiggy delivery handover
name: ch05_rain_delivery_thanks
alt: Late on a rainy night, a soaked delivery rider hands over a food bag at an apartment door; the resident smiles and thanks him, and he walks back to his bike looking a little lighter.
scene: A night scene at the doorway of a Bengaluru apartment in heavy rain, framed from a slight angle so the corridor and the street below are both visible. On the RIGHT, a resident (about 30, home T-shirt and pyjamas, warm light spilling from the open door behind) takes a plain insulated delivery bag in one hand and with the other gives a small grateful wave, smiling warmly; a speech bubble shows a small heart and a motorbike with a careful-road sign. In the CENTRE, the delivery rider (about 25, dripping rain jacket, helmet pushed up, a plain coloured delivery box on his back with no logo) stands soaked, shoulders slumped from a long day, a small phone screen in his hand showing the number "20" for his twentieth order. A small inset bubble above him shows his shoulders lifting and a faint smile. On the LEFT, down on the wet street under a yellow streetlight, the same rider is walking back to his parked motorbike, back a little straighter, a small light glow around him and a dashed arrow from the door to the bike. Rain streaks across the whole scene, puddles reflect the streetlight, cool blue night with the warm doorway as the bright spot. Label: "LIGHTER" above the rider walking back to his bike.
